docs.title: WOMM
docs.text: Works On My Machine — a command-line tool that creates Python and JavaScript projects from templates, configures existing ones, and keeps the small things around them under control: your PATH, the Windows context menu, and the runtimes your work depends on.

docs.title: 🚀 Quick start
docs.text:
Install the tool, then create a project that is ready to run — virtual environment, dependencies and git included.

uv tool install womm-cli
womm create official/python ./hello-womm --setup

Get started walks through it step by step, including what to do when womm is not found after the install.

docs.title: Breaking Changes
docs.text: • womm create <language> is replaced by womm create <template>, with no compatibility alias. Project scaffolding now renders through Copier exclusively: womm create official/python <destination> and womm create official/javascript <destination> replace the old womm create python/womm create javascript/womm create react-ts subcommands. The legacy .template-file engine, its template_utils helpers, and the src/womm/assets/languages/**/templates/ assets have been removed entirely. Use womm template list to discover available catalog templates.

docs.title: Why is the package called womm-cli and the command womm?
docs.text: The name womm was already taken on PyPI by an unrelated project, so the package is published as womm-cli. You only ever type that name when you install or upgrade. Everything else — the command, the repository, the data directory — is womm.

docs.title: Do I need Python installed?
docs.text: No. uv tool install womm-cli downloads the Python version WOMM needs and keeps it in its own isolated environment. Your system Python, if you have one, is left alone.

docs.title: Does WOMM install Python, Node.js or git for me?
docs.text: No. It reports what is available with womm deps check and leaves the installing to you — see Dependencies. Inside a project it does install, when you ask: virtual environment and dependencies.

docs.title: Does WOMM change my PATH on its own?
docs.text: No. Your PATH changes only when you run womm path add or womm path remove, and each of those takes a backup first. The installer does not touch it either: uv tool update-shell is a command you choose to run.

docs.title: Is WOMM Windows-only?
docs.text: No. womm context and womm system refresh-env are Windows-only because they act on the registry and the Windows environment. Everything else works on Windows, macOS and Linux.

docs.title: Where does WOMM keep my data, and does an upgrade erase it?
docs.text: In ~/.womm, and no. Upgrading or uninstalling the program leaves your templates, backups and logs untouched — see Your WOMM data.

docs.title: Can I use a template hosted on a git repository?
docs.text: Not yet. womm template add takes a local directory. Clone the template first, then register the clone.

docs.title: How do I upgrade or remove WOMM?
docs.text:
uv tool upgrade womm-cli
uv tool uninstall womm-cli

Neither touches ~/.womm.

docs.title: Get started with WOMM
docs.text: By the end of this page you will have WOMM installed and a Python project created from a template, with its virtual environment, its dependencies and a git repository already in place.

docs.title: 🔧 Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Windows, macOS or Linux.

  • uv. If you do not have it:

    powershell -ExecutionPolicy ByPass -c "irm https://astral.sh/uv/install.ps1 | iex"   # Windows
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh                                      # macOS, Linux

Python is not a prerequisite

uv tool install downloads the Python version WOMM needs. You do not have to install Python yourself.

docs.title: 📝 Steps
docs.text:
1. Install WOMM as an isolated tool:

    uv tool install womm-cli

    The command is named womm. The package is named womm-cli because the name womm was already taken on PyPI.

  2. If your shell answers womm: command not found, add the tool directory to your PATH, then open a new terminal:

    uv tool update-shell

  3. Check what WOMM sees:

    womm doctor

    The report shows the version, the executable your shell resolves, and the data directory WOMM will use.

  4. Create your first project:

    womm create official/python ./hello-womm --setup

    WOMM asks for the project name, the package name, the Python version and the options of the template. --setup prepares the environment once the files are written: virtual environment, dependencies, git repository.

docs.title: ✅ Result
docs.text: ./hello-womm holds a complete Python project: pyproject.toml with ruff and ty configured, a test suite, a GitHub Actions workflow, and a .venv ready to use. Running womm doctor again shows the same installation, unchanged — WOMM keeps its own data in ~/.womm and never writes into your projects after creation.

docs.title: Release notes
docs.text: What changed for you, newest version first. The full technical history, commit by commit, is in the changelog.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• womm template add copies your template into ~/.womm and renders from the copy, so moving or archiving the original no longer breaks the entry. womm template update NAME refreshes the copy from the original, and remove deletes the copy. Entries registered earlier keep pointing at their directory until you update them.
  • Template identifiers are restricted to letters, digits, ., _ and - in each part, since they now name directories.

docs.title: New
docs.text:
• womm template add, init, update and remove take -I. WOMM asks for missing arguments, shows what it is about to write and waits for your confirmation; init -I offers to register the new skeleton.
  • A user template identifier can carry one namespace, such as neuraaak/my-python-project. official and user are reserved.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• A user template kept in a git repository is rendered from its current state, uncommitted changes included and announced in a warning. It was rendered from its latest tag, silently ignoring later commits.
  • womm create --setup works with user templates that declare _womm.setup.language, and a user template named like an official one no longer receives the official setup.
  • womm template list and show follow edits to a user template's copier.yml without re-registering it, and copier.yaml is accepted.
  • womm template init writes the description you give into the skeleton's catalog metadata, and the skeleton renders a README instead of a stray .gitkeep.
  • The official templates check the project name when you answer: Python requires a valid distribution name and JavaScript a valid npm name. A name such as My Project used to break uv sync or npm install afterwards.
  • womm template init refuses a template name that womm template add would refuse, instead of writing a README with commands that fail.
  • womm setup titles its summary "Incomplete" when a step failed, instead of "Completed!" above the failure warnings.

docs.title: New
docs.text:
• Official Python templates offer Ruff or Black + isort, and ty, mypy or Pyright. JavaScript templates offer Biome or ESLint + Prettier where supported, with optional Knip. Test coverage is optional in both templates.
  • Generated projects record their template provenance and allow tool patches within the tested minor version. Lockfiles retain the exact resolved versions.
  • womm setup --update updates declared tooling and reviewed configurations in official projects. Preview with --dry-run; block moves and destructive migrations require --allow-destructive-actions. Unknown transitions and conflicting values require manual review. Updates retain backups and a separate history; a failed installation restores files but may leave the environment needing synchronization. See Update project tooling.

docs.title: New
docs.text: • WOMM tells you when a newer version is published. A command run in a terminal ends with a line naming the new version and the command that upgrades your installation, and womm run alone shows whether you are up to date under its welcome panel. PyPI is checked at most once a day; set WOMM_NO_UPDATE_CHECK to turn the check off. See Files and variables.

docs.title: Improved
docs.text:
• WOMM starts faster. womm --version, -h and every command run without its arguments answer in about 0.2 s instead of 1.4 s; the other commands save about 0.7 s.
  • A command run without the arguments it requires, such as womm create, shows its help instead of a Missing argument error.

docs.title: 5.1.0 — 2026-11-24
docs.text:
Read before upgrading

  • Python projects managed by uv are set up with uv. On a project with a uv.lock or a [tool.uv] table, womm setup python and womm create --setup run uv sync instead of venv and pip: the installed versions are those of the lockfile, and uv must be on your PATH.
  • womm setup writes nothing without an option. The VS Code configuration it used to write on every run is now the --setup-vscode step of womm setup python and womm setup javascript. womm setup detect detects the project and lists the steps; use -I for the guided setup.

docs.title: Improved
docs.text:
• womm setup python and womm setup javascript run without options list the available step options instead of reporting a completed setup.
  • womm create without --setup tells you how to prepare the environment.
  • -h works on every command, womm context, womm deps and womm system included.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Python projects created with uv (the template default) pass their own CI after womm create --setup: it now writes the uv.lock the workflow requires, instead of a pip install without a lockfile.
  • --setup uses the Python version the project asks for: a project needing a newer Python than WOMM's own was left without its dependencies.
  • Python projects set up with pip are installed in editable mode, so code changes are visible without reinstalling.
  • The GitHub Actions workflow of the Python template uses the current setup-uv and setup-python releases.

docs.title: 5.0.0 — 2026-11-24
docs.text:
Read before upgrading

  • --setup-dev-tools is gone from womm setup python and womm setup javascript; Click now rejects it. Use --install-deps, which already installs the development dependencies the project declares.

docs.title: Improved
docs.text:
• womm create --setup and womm setup javascript --install-deps install with the project's own package manager: the packageManager field of package.json, then its lockfile, and npm otherwise. They no longer force npm on pnpm, Yarn or Bun projects.
  • On a Python project, --setup-git-hooks now also runs pre-commit install when the project has a .pre-commit-config.yaml, with the pre-commit of its virtual environment.
  • The setup summary lists only the steps that actually ran.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• On Windows, womm create official/javascript --setup installed nothing.
  • Projects generated from the JavaScript template pass their own CI again: the Biome configuration was rejected, Vue projects failed the format check, Yarn projects linted Yarn's own files, and ESLint crashed on Vue projects installed with Yarn.
  • womm setup javascript no longer adds ESLint, Prettier, Husky and lint-staged on top of the toolchain the template ships.

docs.title: 4.0.0 — 2026-10-29
docs.text:
Read before upgrading

This version changes how you install WOMM, how you create projects, and what WOMM does with data left by older installations. The three points below need an action from you.

  • Install with uv or pip. The self-installer and the standalone installer are gone. Install with uv tool install womm-cli, upgrade with uv tool upgrade womm-cli. The womm install and womm uninstall commands no longer exist.
  • womm create takes a template, not a language. Use womm create official/python <destination> instead of womm create python. womm template list shows what is available. There is no compatibility alias.
  • Data left by an older self-installed WOMM is no longer migrated. If your ~/.womm still holds .logs, .templates, .backup or .proof, they stay where they are and are ignored. Move what you want to keep into logs/, templates/ and backups/ yourself.

docs.title: New
docs.text:
• womm doctor reports what your installation resolves — version, command, data directory, context menu entries — and changes nothing.
  • womm template manages a catalog: list and inspect entries, register your own template under user/, scaffold a new one with womm template init.
  • womm create accepts --pretend to simulate a render, --data KEY=VALUE to pre-fill one answer, and --setup to prepare the environment right after.
  • womm path backup takes, lists, shows and restores PATH snapshots, and a snapshot is now taken automatically before every PATH change.
  • womm context backup cherry-pick restores only the context menu entries you select.
  • womm deps reports both strata — runtimes and runtime package managers — with versions, and exits non-zero when a requirement is missing.

docs.title: Improved
docs.text:
• Projects are rendered with Copier, so templates ask real questions and you can register your own.
  • The official Python template targets Python 3.13 and 3.14, with ruff, ty, pytest, pre-commit and a pinned GitHub Actions workflow; Django is optional and reads its secret key from the environment.
  • The official JavaScript template targets Node.js 24 and 26, with Biome (ESLint and Prettier for Vue), Vite, Vitest, and the package manager of your choice.
  • ~/.womm holds data only — logs, templates and backups — never code.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• A project description containing a quote, a backslash, { or < no longer breaks the generated pyproject.toml, package.json, React and Vue components, or Python docstring.
  • A generated Django project writes its database at the project root instead of inside src/, and ignores it in git.
  • Generated projects derive their version from the package itself, so pyproject.toml and __init__.py cannot drift apart.

docs.title: Removed
docs.text:
• womm lint and womm spell — linting and spell checking belong to the project's own tooling, which the templates already configure.
  • --log-level, --log-file and --log-json. They were accepted but never applied the setting they promised; Click now rejects them.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: One entry per problem, named as you would describe it.

docs.title: womm is not found after the install
docs.text:
Symptom — uv tool install womm-cli succeeded, but your shell answers womm: command not found or 'womm' is not recognized.

Cause — uv installs the command as a shim in ~/.local/bin, and that directory is not on your PATH yet.

Fix

  1. Let uv add it:

    uv tool update-shell

  2. Open a new terminal. On Windows you can refresh the current one instead:

    womm system refresh-env

  3. Still nothing? Call the shim directly to confirm the install itself is fine — ~/.local/bin/womm --version — then check your shell profile for a line that resets PATH.

docs.title: The destination is not empty
docs.text:
Symptom — womm create stops with Destination is not empty, and lists what it found.

Cause — WOMM refuses to render into a directory that already holds files, so it cannot silently mix a template with your work.

Fix

  1. Render into a fresh directory, or

  2. Preview what a merge would write:

    womm create official/python ./my-app --pretend --force

  3. If the result is what you want, run the same command without --pretend. Files produced by the template replace their counterparts; everything else is left alone.

docs.title: womm setup detect picks the wrong language
docs.text:
Symptom — the detection reports a project type you did not expect, or exits with No suitable project type detected.

Cause — detection reads the markers in the directory (pyproject.toml, package.json, and so on). A mixed or empty project leaves it undecided.

Fix — name the language yourself:

womm setup python
womm setup javascript --type react

docs.title: womm template add says "not a Copier template"
docs.text:
Symptom — registering a directory fails with Not a Copier template.

Cause — the source has no copier.yml or copier.yaml at its root, or it is a remote URL, which is not supported yet.

Fix

  1. Check that the directory holds a copier.yml or copier.yaml.
  2. For a remote template, clone it first, then register the clone.

  3. To start a template from scratch, let WOMM scaffold one:

    womm template init ./templates/my-template

docs.title: A command fails on a missing runtime
docs.text:
Symptom — a --setup or womm setup step fails, saying a runtime or package manager is unavailable.

Cause — WOMM reports dependencies, it never installs them.

Fix

  1. See what is missing:

    womm deps check -v

  2. Install it with your own package manager (winget, Homebrew, apt, or the vendor installer).

  3. On Windows, refresh the environment, then run the command again:

    womm system refresh-env

docs.title: A new PATH entry is not visible
docs.text:
Symptom — womm path list shows the directory, but your other programs cannot find the executable.

Cause — a process reads the PATH when it starts. The terminal and the programs already open still hold the old one.

Fix

  1. On Windows, refresh the current terminal:

    womm system refresh-env

  2. Otherwise, open a new terminal. Programs started before the change need to be restarted too.

docs.title: A context menu entry does not appear
docs.text:
Symptom — womm context register succeeded, but the entry is missing when you right-click.

Cause — the entry was registered for another scope than the one you are testing: the background of a folder, a drive, a single file and a multiple selection are four different places.

Fix

  1. Check what is registered, and for which scope:

    womm context list

  2. Register the scope you actually use — for example the folder background:

    womm context register --target "C:\tools\build.ps1" --label "Build project" --background

  3. If an entry has to go, remove it by its registry key name:

    womm context unregister --remove "Build project"

docs.title: womm doctor says the data directory is not writable
docs.text:
Symptom — the report shows Data directory: … (not writable).

Cause — ~/.womm (or the path in WOMM_HOME) belongs to another user, sits on a read-only volume, or is blocked by a policy.

Fix

  1. Check the owner and permissions of the directory the report prints.

  2. Or point WOMM somewhere you own:

    setx WOMM_HOME "D:\womm-data"      # Windows, new terminals
export WOMM_HOME="$HOME/womm-data" # macOS, Linux

  3. Run womm doctor again to confirm.

docs.title: A womm context or refresh-env command does nothing
docs.text:
Symptom — on macOS or Linux, these commands have no effect.

Cause — both act on Windows mechanisms: the registry for the context menu, and the Windows environment for refresh-env.

Fix — none needed: they are Windows-only by design. Every other command works on all three platforms.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
WOMM needs external programs to do its work, and it sorts them into two strata.

Runtimes come first: Python 3.13 or later, Node.js 18 or later, and git 2.30 or later. They are the programs a project is built on.

Runtime package managers come second: pip and uv for Python, npm and yarn for Node.js. Each one depends on its runtime — uv is only useful once Python is there.

The two strata are hierarchical, which is why womm deps check succeeds only when every runtime is installed and at least one package manager is available: a runtime without a package manager cannot install anything.

docs.title: WOMM never installs them
docs.text:
womm deps reports, it does not install. Installing a runtime touches your whole machine, often needs administrator rights, and every operating system does it differently — so that decision stays yours. Use your own package manager (winget, Homebrew, apt, or the installer from the vendor).

What WOMM does install is inside a project: a virtual environment and the project's own dependencies, when you ask for them with --setup or womm setup.

docs.title: The template catalog
docs.text:
The catalog is the list of templates WOMM can render. It has two origins, and both appear in womm template list.

Official templates ship inside WOMM itself. There are two — official/python and official/javascript — and they are read-only: they are updated when you upgrade WOMM, never by you.

User templates are directories on your machine that you register under the user/ namespace. WOMM keeps its own copy of each one and renders from it, so your directory can move or be archived; womm template update refreshes the copy from it. Your files are never modified.

Every template is a Copier template: a copier.yml declaring the questions, and a template/ directory whose files are rendered with your answers. womm create asks those questions and writes the result; it adds the catalog and the environment setup around Copier, nothing more.

A template source must be a local directory. A git URL is not supported yet.

docs.title: ➡️ Next steps
docs.text:
• Manage templates — register, scaffold, update or drop an entry.
  • Create a project — render an entry.

docs.title: Your WOMM data
docs.text:
WOMM's installation data lives in one directory: ~/.womm — that is C:\Users\<you>\.womm on Windows. It holds data only, never code.

Inside ~/.womm What it holds logs/ The log files of past runs templates/ The catalog of your templates, and WOMM's copies of them backups/path/ PATH snapshots, taken before every PATH change backups/registry/ Windows context menu snapshots update-check.json The last WOMM release seen on PyPI

Three consequences worth knowing:

  • Upgrading or removing WOMM does not touch it. uv tool upgrade womm-cli and uv tool uninstall womm-cli replace or remove the program; your templates, backups and logs stay.
  • It is yours to inspect. The backups are plain JSON files, so you can read one without WOMM if you ever need to.
  • You can move it. Set the WOMM_HOME environment variable to another absolute path and WOMM uses that directory instead — useful to keep a project machine isolated, or to test without touching your real data.

There is no settings file: WOMM has no persistent configuration of its own. Behaviour is decided by the command and its options, every time.

Explicit womm setup --update operations keep project-specific history in .womm-update.json and backups in .womm-backups/update/ inside that project. These stay with the project and are separate from the installation data above. The original .womm-template.json remains the record of how it was generated.

docs.title: ➡️ Next steps

  • Diagnose your installation — check the directory WOMM resolves and whether it is writable.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text: Every command, as womm --help reports it. -h, --help works on each one, and -v, --verbose on most.

docs.title: Projects
docs.text: Command What it does womm create TEMPLATE DEST Render a catalog template into DEST womm setup detect Detect the project type, list its steps womm setup python Configure an existing Python project womm setup javascript Configure an existing JavaScript project womm setup --update Update official project tooling after confirmation

docs.title: womm create options
docs.text: Option Effect --data KEY=VALUE Pre-fill one template answer. Repeatable. --defaults Use the template defaults instead of prompting. --force Render into a destination that is not empty. --pretend Simulate the rendering, write nothing. --setup Prepare the environment after rendering. -v, --verbose Show the detailed output.

docs.title: womm setup options
docs.text:
Option detect python javascript -p, --path DIRECTORY yes yes yes -I, --interactive yes yes yes -v, --verbose yes yes yes --install-deps no yes yes --setup-git-hooks no yes yes --setup-vscode no yes yes --virtual-env no yes no -t, --type TYPE no no yes

The update mode takes --path DIRECTORY, --dry-run and --allow-destructive-actions. These options belong directly after setup and cannot be combined with its subcommands. --dry-run resolves dependencies in a temporary copy without applying the update. --allow-destructive-actions permits reviewed structural migrations, never ambiguous conflicts or unknown version transitions. See Update an official project's tooling.

docs.title: Templates
docs.text:
Command What it does womm template list List every catalog entry, official first womm template show IDENTIFIER Show one entry in detail womm template add NAME SOURCE Copy a local template and register it under user/ womm template init DESTINATION Scaffold a new Copier template skeleton womm template update NAME [SOURCE] Copy a user entry again, from SOURCE if given womm template remove NAME Unregister a user entry and delete its copy

womm template init also takes --data KEY=VALUE, --defaults and --force.

add, init, update and remove take -I / --interactive: WOMM asks for the arguments you leave out, shows what it is about to write and asks you to confirm. init -I then offers to register the new skeleton.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text: Command What it does womm deps check Probe both strata; exit 0 when the requirements are met womm deps status Full status table, with versions womm deps list Static inventory of what WOMM knows about

docs.title: PATH
docs.text: Command What it does womm path list List the entries of your current PATH womm path add DIRECTORY Add a directory that exists and holds an executable womm path remove DIRECTORY Remove an entry, existing or not womm path backup create Snapshot the current PATH womm path backup list List the snapshots womm path backup show NAME Print the content of one snapshot womm path backup restore [NAME] Restore a snapshot; interactive without NAME

docs.title: Windows context menu
docs.text: Command What it does womm context quick-setup Register the usual WOMM entries womm context register Register your own entry (see options below) womm context list List the registered entries womm context unregister --remove KEY Remove one entry by its registry key name womm context backup create Snapshot the current entries womm context backup list List the snapshots womm context backup show NAME Print the content of one snapshot womm context backup restore NAME Restore a snapshot womm context backup cherry-pick Restore only the entries you select

docs.title: womm context register options
docs.text: Option Effect --target PATH Script or executable the entry launches -l, --label TEXT Label shown in the menu --icon TEXT Icon path, or auto to take it from the target (default) --background Register for the background of a folder --root Register for drives --file Register for a single selected file -F, --files Register for a multiple file selection --file-types TEXT Register for a family of types, such as image or text --extension TEXT Register for given extensions, such as .py or .js -I, --interactive Guided setup

docs.title: System and diagnostic
docs.text: Command What it does womm doctor Report the installed runtime; changes nothing womm system detect Detect system information and available tools womm system refresh-env Refresh the environment variables (Windows only) womm --version Print the version

docs.title: Data directory
docs.text:
Path Content Created ~/.womm/ Everything WOMM keeps for you On first use ~/.womm/logs/ Log files of past runs On first use ~/.womm/templates/ Catalog of your registered templates On first registration ~/.womm/backups/path/ PATH snapshots, named .path_<YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS>.json Before every PATH change ~/.womm/backups/registry/ Context menu snapshots, named context_menu_backup_<YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS>.json On backup ~/.womm/update-check.json Latest release seen on PyPI and when it was checked On first update check

On Windows, ~ is C:\Users\<you>.

WOMM never writes code into this directory. Explicit setup and tooling-update commands can write into a project after creation.

docs.title: Project update files
docs.text:
Path Content .womm-template.json Original generation provenance; preserved by updates .womm-update.json Successful tooling updates, versions and migrations .womm-backups/update/<id>/ Previous files and a manifest naming files originally absent .womm-update.lock Exclusive apply lock; removed when the update finishes

Ignore .womm-backups/ and .womm-update.lock in Git. Backups are local to the project and can contain local configuration. A preview creates none of these files. See Update tooling for migration boundaries and recovery after a failed installation.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text: Variable Effect Default WOMM_HOME Absolute path used as the data directory instead of ~/.womm ~/.womm WOMM_NO_UPDATE_CHECK Any non-empty value turns off the new-release notice Unset

docs.title: New-release notice
docs.text:
When a newer WOMM is published on PyPI, a command run in a terminal ends with a yellow line on stderr naming the new version and the command that upgrades your installation, such as uv tool upgrade womm-cli. Run alone, womm shows the same check under its welcome panel, and says so when WOMM is up to date. WOMM never upgrades itself.

PyPI is asked at most once a day; the answer is kept in ~/.womm/update-check.json. Without a network the check gives up after one second and is not retried before the next day. It never runs when the output is not a terminal, when the CI variable is set, or when WOMM_NO_UPDATE_CHECK is set.

docs.title: Settings file
docs.text: There is none. WOMM has no persistent configuration: every behaviour is decided by the command and its options.

docs.title: Installed files
docs.text: Installed with uv tool install womm-cli, the program lives in uv's tool directory and the womm command is a shim in ~/.local/bin. Neither is meant to be edited; uv tool upgrade womm-cli replaces them.

docs.title: Guides
docs.text: One page per task, in the order you usually meet them.

docs.title: 📝 Projects
docs.text: Task When you need it Create a project Start a new Python or JavaScript project from a template Configure an existing project Add an environment and tooling to a project you already have Manage templates List the catalog, register your own template, build a new one

docs.title: 📝 Your machine
docs.text: Task When you need it Check what WOMM needs Find out which runtimes and package managers are available Manage your PATH Add or remove a directory, and undo it from a backup Use the Windows context menu Right-click entries for your tools, and their backups Diagnose your installation Check what WOMM resolves, and refresh your environment

docs.title: Check what WOMM needs
docs.text: Find out which runtimes and package managers are available on your machine before WOMM uses them.

docs.title: 🔧 Prerequisites
docs.text:
• WOMM installed — see Get started.

WOMM installs nothing

These commands only report. Installing a missing runtime is up to you and your operating system's package manager — see Dependencies.

docs.title: 📝 Steps
docs.text:
1. Check availability:

    womm deps check

    The exit status is 0 when every runtime is installed and at least one runtime package manager is available. Add -v to see the version of each component.

  2. See the full picture in one table:

    womm deps status

  3. See what WOMM knows about, independently of your machine:

    womm deps list

docs.title: ✅ Result
docs.text:
You know which of the runtimes (Python, Node.js, git) and which runtime package managers (pip, uv, npm, yarn) WOMM can rely on, and which ones you need to install yourself.

A command that fails on a missing runtime is covered in Troubleshooting.

docs.title: ➡️ Next steps
docs.text:
• Dependencies — why there are two strata and why WOMM never installs.
  • Diagnose your installation — what WOMM itself resolves.

docs.title: Configure an existing project
docs.text: Add a development environment and tooling to a project you already have, without re-creating it from a template.

docs.title: 🔧 Prerequisites
docs.text:
• WOMM installed — see Get started.
  • An existing project directory.
  • The runtime of the project available: Python for a Python project, Node.js for a JavaScript one. See Check what WOMM needs.

docs.title: 📝 Steps
docs.text:
1. Let WOMM detect the project type. It shows the steps available for it and writes nothing:

    cd my-existing-project
womm setup detect

  2. Or name the language yourself:

    womm setup python
womm setup javascript

  3. Choose what to prepare. Every step is opt-in: run the command with the options for the steps you want, and nothing else happens.

    womm setup python --virtual-env --install-deps

    Run without options, WOMM detects and validates the project, writes nothing, and lists the options of the available steps.

  4. To be guided question by question, use the interactive mode:

    womm setup python --interactive

docs.title: ⚙️ Options
docs.text: Option Effect Available on -p, --path DIRECTORY Work on this directory instead of the current one. detect, python, javascript -I, --interactive Guided setup, one question at a time. detect, python, javascript -v, --verbose Show the detailed output. detect, python, javascript --install-deps Install the project dependencies, dev ones included. python, javascript --setup-git-hooks Initialize git; on Python, install pre-commit hooks. python, javascript --setup-vscode Write the VS Code settings and recommended extensions. python, javascript --virtual-env Create the virtual environment. python -t, --type TYPE Force the project type: javascript, react or vue. javascript

docs.title: ✅ Result
docs.text:
The project has the environment and the tooling you asked for. WOMM reports each step it ran and what it skipped.

A JavaScript project is installed with the package manager it declares: the packageManager field of package.json, then its lockfile, and npm otherwise. WOMM adds no linter, formatter or git hook of its own.

A Python project with a uv.lock or a [tool.uv] table in its pyproject.toml is set up with uv: uv sync --group dev, or uv venv with --virtual-env alone. uv picks the Python version the project asks for and writes uv.lock; it must be on your PATH. Any other Python project gets a virtual environment and an editable pip install.

On a Python project, --setup-git-hooks also runs pre-commit install when the project has a .pre-commit-config.yaml, with the pre-commit of its virtual environment: combine it with --install-deps so that pre-commit is there.

If detection picks the wrong language, name it explicitly with womm setup python or womm setup javascript — see Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Update an official project's tooling
docs.text:
For a project generated from an official template with a .womm-template.json file, upgrade WOMM, then preview the tools and configurations it can update:

womm setup --update --path ./my-project --dry-run
womm setup --update --path ./my-project

WOMM reads the project's installed or locked versions, resolves the target versions in a temporary copy, applies its migration registry and validates the configuration with the target tools. The preview may download dependencies and use package-manager caches; it leaves the original project and environment unchanged. Applying shows the plan and asks for confirmation.

Only development tools still declared in the project are managed. Removed tools are not added back. Application code, generation choices and the original .womm-template.json are preserved. Tool constraints follow the current WOMM template; the native lockfile records the resolved versions. Python supports uv and project-local pip environments; JavaScript supports npm, pnpm, modern Yarn and Bun. Yarn Classic requires manual review. Workspaces, conditional Python tooling requirements and URL requirements need manual review.

By default, reviewed scalar key moves preserve their value. Moving a list or table, removing a key or changing a configuration value requires explicit consent:

womm setup --update --dry-run --allow-destructive-actions
womm setup --update --allow-destructive-actions

The flag permits only known migrations. Conflicting destination values and unregistered version transitions still block the entire update. Same-minor patch updates are supported; crossing a minor boundary needs a reviewed registry entry. The initial registry includes Ruff's legacy lint settings and Biome's native v1-to-v2 migrator for the shipped target range. This is not a universal configuration migrator. Run your project's lint, tests and build after updating.

Before applying, WOMM stores the previous files in .womm-backups/update/<id>/. Add .womm-backups/ and .womm-update.lock to your project's .gitignore; backups can contain your local configuration. .womm-update.json records successful updates separately from generation provenance. If installation fails, WOMM restores the files and retains the backup. The environment may be partially updated: synchronize it using the restored manifest and lockfile. Pip has no persistent full dependency lock.

docs.title: ➡️ Next steps
docs.text: • Check what WOMM needs — when a step fails for a missing runtime.

docs.title: Create a project
docs.text: Start a new project from a template in the catalog. WOMM asks the template's questions, writes the files, and optionally prepares the environment.

docs.title: 🔧 Prerequisites
docs.text:
• WOMM installed — see Get started.
  • A template identifier. womm template list shows the catalog; official/python and official/javascript ship with WOMM.
  • For --setup: the runtime of the project (Python or Node.js) available on your machine. WOMM reports what is missing but installs nothing — see Check what WOMM needs.

docs.title: 📝 Steps
docs.text:
1. Pick a template and a destination:

    womm create official/python ./my-app

  2. Answer the questions. Each template asks its own: project name, package name, minimum Python version, framework, license, and whether to include tests, coverage, CI and shared editor settings. The official templates also let you choose the linting, formatting and type-checking tools.

  3. To also prepare the environment after rendering, add --setup:

    womm create official/python ./my-app --setup

    This creates the virtual environment, installs the dependencies and initializes git.

docs.title: ⚙️ Options
docs.text:
Option Effect --data KEY=VALUE Pre-fill one answer, so it is not asked. Repeatable. --defaults Take the template defaults instead of prompting. --force Render into a destination that is not empty. Merges, see below. --pretend Simulate: show what would be written, write nothing. --setup Prepare the environment after rendering. -v, --verbose Show the detailed output.

Pre-filling and taking the defaults combine well for a scripted creation:

womm create official/javascript ./web --defaults \
  --data project_name=web --data framework=react --data typescript=true

docs.title: Choose development tools
docs.text:
Template Answer Choices Python tooling ruff (recommended), black-isort Python type_checker ty (recommended), mypy, pyright JavaScript/TypeScript tooling biome (recommended for plain JS/TS and React), eslint-prettier JavaScript/TypeScript with_knip true to check unused files, exports and dependencies; default false Both with_coverage Include coverage when tests are enabled; default true for Python, false for JS/TS

Vue uses ESLint + Prettier; the template refuses Biome for this profile. The Python black-isort profile keeps Ruff for linting and delegates formatting and import sorting to Black and isort. The generated configurations, CI, hooks, editor recommendations and README all follow your choices.

womm create official/python ./my-app --defaults \
  --data project_name=my-app --data tooling=black-isort --data type_checker=mypy

womm create official/javascript ./web --defaults \
  --data project_name=web --data framework=react --data typescript=true \
  --data tooling=eslint-prettier --data with_knip=true --data with_coverage=true

--force merges, it does not overwrite everything

--force allows rendering into a non-empty directory. Files the template produces replace their counterparts; everything else is left in place. Run the same command with --pretend first if you are unsure what it touches.

docs.title: ✅ Result
docs.text:
The destination holds the rendered project. With --setup, the environment is ready and git is initialized.

The official templates record the WOMM version, template identifier and version, and original choices in .womm-template.json. This file describes how the project was generated; it is not an inventory of the current environment or a Copier update file. To change an answer, create again into another destination.

docs.title: Keep tools and configurations compatible
docs.text:
Tools whose configurations are generated allow patches within the same minor, starting at the tested version. For example, Python's ruff~=0.17.2 allows >=0.17.2,<0.18.0, and JavaScript's ~2.6.8 allows >=2.6.8,<2.7.0. Ruff's required-version enforces the same range. With coverage enabled, Vitest and its coverage provider keep matching exact versions.

Biome uses the schema from its installed package. Yarn Plug'n'Play omits the $schema reference because there is no node_modules path; Biome still validates the configuration. Install the project's dependencies and run its local tools rather than global copies. Commit the lockfile and use it in CI: it records exact resolved versions, so frozen installs stay reproducible.

Patch updates require an explicit lockfile update. Before moving to another minor, review the tool's release notes, update its dependency range and any matching schema or version guard, adapt the configuration, update the lockfile, then run the project's format, lint, type, test and build checks. The generated README gives commands for the chosen tools and package manager. Pip projects have no generated lockfile; their constraints alone do not lock dependencies.

Upgrading WOMM changes the templates used for future projects. It does not migrate existing projects or update their configurations.

If the command stops on a non-empty destination or on a missing runtime, see Troubleshooting.

docs.title: ➡️ Next steps
docs.text:
• Manage templates — register your own template.
  • The template catalog — official and user templates, and where the catalog lives.

docs.title: Diagnose your installation
docs.text: Check what WOMM resolves on your machine — version, executable, data directory — and refresh your environment after a change.

docs.title: 🔧 Prerequisites
docs.text: • WOMM installed — see Get started.

docs.title: 📝 Steps
docs.text:
1. Ask WOMM about itself:

    womm doctor

    The report lists the version, the womm command your shell resolves, the data directory and whether it is writable, and the number of registered context menu entries. Add -v to also see the resolved executable path. The command changes nothing.

  2. Ask WOMM about your machine:

    womm system detect

  3. On Windows, after installing a tool or changing your PATH, refresh the environment without opening a new terminal:

    womm system refresh-env

docs.title: ✅ Result
docs.text:
You know which installation of WOMM is answering, where its data lives, and which tools it can see. Nothing on your machine was modified.

If womm doctor reports a data directory that is not writable, or no womm on your PATH, see Troubleshooting.

docs.title: ➡️ Next steps
docs.text:
• Check what WOMM needs — the runtimes behind the commands.
  • Your WOMM data — what lives in the data directory.

docs.title: Manage templates
docs.text: Inspect the template catalog, register a template of your own, or scaffold a new one from scratch.

docs.title: 🔧 Prerequisites
docs.text:
• WOMM installed — see Get started.
  • To register a template: a local directory holding a copier.yml (or copier.yaml) file. Remote sources (a git URL) are not supported yet.
  • To scaffold one: nothing more. womm template init writes the skeleton.

docs.title: List and inspect
docs.text:
womm template list
womm template show official/python

list shows every entry with its version and description, official ones first. show prints one entry in detail. A short name works when it is unambiguous: womm template show python.

docs.title: Register your own
docs.text:
womm template add mytpl ./templates/my-template

WOMM copies the directory into ~/.womm/templates/copies/ and renders from that copy, so moving, renaming or archiving the original breaks nothing. Everything is copied except .git: register a clean template directory, not one holding a .venv or node_modules.

The identifier is a name, optionally prefixed by one namespace of your own: mytpl or neuraaak/mytpl. WOMM files it under the user/ origin, so these are listed as user/mytpl and user/neuraaak/mytpl. official and user are reserved and cannot be used as a namespace. Each part names a directory of the copy: letters, digits, ., _ and -, starting and ending with a letter or digit.

Prefer to be guided? womm template add -I asks for the identifier and the directory, shows the entry it read from copier.yml, and registers it only once you confirm. update -I and remove -I let you pick the entry from a list.

Edited your template since? womm template update mytpl copies it again from the directory it was registered from; show -v names that directory.

To let womm create --setup prepare projects made from your template, declare their language in copier.yml:

_womm:
  setup:
    language: python  # or javascript

docs.title: Scaffold a new template
docs.text:
womm template init ./templates/my-template

WOMM renders a Copier template skeleton: a copier.yml, a template/ directory and the metadata the catalog needs. --data KEY=VALUE, --defaults and --force behave as in Create a project. With -I, WOMM asks for the destination if you leave it out, then offers to register the skeleton in the catalog.

docs.title: Refresh an entry, move it, or drop it
docs.text:
womm template update mytpl                          # copy again from its origin
womm template update mytpl ./templates/my-template-v2  # copy from a new origin
womm template remove mytpl

If the origin has moved, update without a directory says so: pass the new location. remove unregisters the entry and deletes WOMM's copy; your template directory stays on disk. Only user entries can be updated or removed — the official ones ship inside WOMM.

An entry registered before WOMM 5.5.0 still points at your directory and is rendered from it directly: if it is a git repository, from its current commit plus uncommitted changes. womm template update turns it into a copy.

docs.title: ✅ Result
docs.text:
womm template list reflects the change, and womm create user/mytpl ./my-app renders your template like any official one.

If add refuses the source, it is missing a copier.yml — see Troubleshooting.

docs.title: ➡️ Next steps
docs.text:
• Create a project — render any catalog entry.
  • The template catalog — where the catalog lives and what official means.

docs.title: Manage your PATH
docs.text: Add or remove a directory from your user PATH, and undo the change from a backup.

docs.title: 🔧 Prerequisites
docs.text:
• WOMM installed — see Get started.
  • For add: a directory that exists and holds at least one executable.

Your PATH is backed up before every change

womm path add and womm path remove back up the current PATH before touching it, so womm path backup restore always has a way back.

docs.title: See what is on your PATH
docs.text: womm path list

docs.title: Add a directory
docs.text:
womm path add "C:\tools\bin"

The directory must exist and contain an executable, otherwise WOMM refuses the change. Open a new terminal to pick up the new PATH — on Windows, womm system refresh-env refreshes it without reopening.

docs.title: Remove a directory
docs.text:
womm path remove "C:\tools\bin"

The directory does not have to exist: dropping the leftover entry of a tool you uninstalled is the usual reason to run this.

docs.title: Undo from a backup
docs.text:
womm path backup list
womm path backup show .path_20261029_120000.json
womm path backup restore .path_20261029_120000.json

restore without a name lets you pick one from the list. show and restore take a bare backup file name, as printed by backup list — not a path.

To take a snapshot before doing something risky by hand:

womm path backup create

docs.title: ✅ Result
docs.text:
womm path list shows the entry added or gone, and womm path backup list shows the backup that was taken just before the change.

If the new entry is not visible to your other programs, see Troubleshooting.

docs.title: ➡️ Next steps
docs.text: • Your WOMM data — where the backups are kept.

docs.title: Use the Windows context menu
docs.text:
Add your own entries to the Windows right-click menu, list what is registered, and restore a previous state from a backup.

Windows only

womm context reads and writes the Windows registry. On macOS and Linux the command group exists but has nothing to act on.

docs.title: 🔧 Prerequisites
docs.text:
• WOMM installed on Windows — see Get started.
  • The script or executable you want to launch from the menu.

docs.title: Register the usual WOMM entries
docs.text: womm context quick-setup

docs.title: Register your own entry
docs.text:
womm context register --target "C:\tools\build.ps1" --label "Build project" --background

Choose where the entry appears with the scope options:

Option Where the entry appears --background Right-click on the empty space inside a folder --root Right-click on a drive --file Right-click on a single selected file -F, --files Right-click on a multiple file selection --file-types Only for a family of types, such as image, text --extension Only for given extensions, such as .py, .js

--icon takes a path or auto (the default) to pick the icon from the target. -I, --interactive walks you through the same choices.

docs.title: See what is registered
docs.text: womm context list

docs.title: Remove an entry
docs.text:
womm context unregister --remove "Build project"

--remove is required and takes the key name as stored in the registry, which womm context list prints.

docs.title: Back up and restore
docs.text:
womm context backup create
womm context backup list
womm context backup show context_menu_backup_20261029_120000.json
womm context backup restore context_menu_backup_20261029_120000.json

To bring back only part of a backup, pick the entries you want:

womm context backup cherry-pick

docs.title: ✅ Result
docs.text:
The entry appears in the right-click menu for the scope you chose, and womm context list counts it. A backup taken before a change can restore the previous state, in full or entry by entry.

If the entry does not show up, see Troubleshooting.

docs.title: ➡️ Next steps
docs.text: • Your WOMM data — where registry backups are kept.
